reason: This passage (Exodus 14) emphasizes God's power, divine deliverance, and the importance of faith and obedience to God's will as the central themes of leadership and salvation. While Moses does not respond defensively when the Israelites criticize him—instead redirecting them to trust in God—the text does not present humility in the face of criticism as the model of good leadership. Rather, the passage focuses on how the true leader (Moses) must faithfully obey God's commands and inspire faith in the divine, while God Himself is portrayed as the ultimate leader and deliverer. The emphasis is on God's strength and the leader's role as God's instrument, not on humility as a leadership virtue.
